html:
The Phrygians were a people of central Anatolia, in today's Turkey, who spoke an Indo-European language related to Greek. The map shows them from 1500 to 700 BCE, but they are thought to have arrived from the Balkans only around 1200 BCE, in the turmoil of the Late Bronze Age collapse, filling the space left by the Hittites.

Their kingdom was strongest in the 700s BCE, with its capital at Gordion. Its best known king was Midas, remembered by the Greeks for the legend of the golden touch and named in Assyrian records as Mita. Huge burial mounds at Gordion show the wealth of its rulers, with fine wooden furniture and bronze vessels.

Around 700 BCE nomad Cimmerians overran the kingdom, and Phrygia later fell under Lydia and then Persia. The Phrygian mother goddess, Matar, lived on as Cybele; in 204 BCE the Romans brought her cult to Rome.
